# C# golden data for the profile store

Frozen output of the C# app's own profile code (`LocalProfileManager`, `SqliteProfileStore`, `StateSyncBroker`
from `apps/windows/src/SubtitleAdder.Core` and `EngineKit` at commit `2f4bc96`), produced by the former fixture
tool `apps/desktop/tools/fixtures/ProfileFixtures` (a .NET 10 console app that linked those sources read-only) on
Windows 11, .NET SDK 10, before the C# app was removed. `tests/win_fixtures.rs` and
`src/mac/tests/csharp_interop.rs` read these files instead of running .NET.

The tool ran with `TMP`/`TEMP` pointing at a scratch folder and a private broker channel. The data folder was
`C:\ProgramData\SubtitleAdderTestFixtures\profiles\data`. The tool keeps media next to the data folder, so the
stored video paths point to `C:\ProgramData\SubtitleAdderTestFixtures\profiles\media\`. The tests recreate those
media files there, with contents from the xorshift32 generator in the tests: `Yaz Tatili Ç.mp4` (5000 bytes,
seed 1), `belgesel-uzay.mp4` (70000, seed 2) and `zeynep_klip.mp4` (1234, seed 3). `missing_episode.mkv` never
exists. Salts, AES-GCM nonces, list ids and times are random, so these files cannot be regenerated byte for byte.
They are the reference as they are.

| File | Tool command | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generate/data/` | `generate <data>` | `profiles.json` + `profiles.db`: Emre (history, likes, ratings, progress, two lists, thumbnails) and zeynep (remembered session) |
| `generate/dump.json` | `dump <copy> Emre pässwörd-1 zeynep z-pass` | What C# read from `generate/data` (on a copy, because a dump logs in) |
| `generate/watch-progress-event.json` | `seal-event <root>\event-data Emre pässwörd-1 <media>\Yaz Tatili Ç.mp4` | A watch-progress event (61.5 / 300) sealed by C# for `generate/data` copied to `C:\ProgramData\SubtitleAdderTestFixtures\profiles\event-data`. Its scope path is part of the AAD, so the test opens the data there |
| `generate-mutate/data/` | `mutate <data>` after `generate` | The second C# step on top of `generate/data` |
| `generate-mutate/dump.json` | `dump <copy> Emre pässwörd-1 zeynep z-pass` | What C# read from `generate-mutate/data` |
| `legacy/data/profiles.json` | `legacy <data>` | A version-2 header with monolithic vaults (eski / eski-şifre, bos / bos-pw) |
| `legacy/dump.json` | `dump <copy> eski eski-şifre bos bos-pw` | What C# read from it |
| `legacy/migrated/` | (the copy after that dump) | The folder as C# migrated it: `profiles.json` v3, `profiles.db`, `profiles.json.bak` |
| `vectors.json` | `vectors` | PBKDF2 / HMAC / owner-tag / list-item-hash / `ToUpperInvariant` / padding vectors, plus a vault marker sealed by C# |
| `fingerprints.json` | `fingerprint <file>` | C# content fingerprints of xorshift32 files (length, seed) that straddle the 64 KiB slices |

The remembered sessions in `generate/data` and `generate-mutate/data` are DPAPI-protected for the Windows account
that ran the tool. `recording-account.json` holds the SHA-256 of that account's user SID (lowercase hex of the
UTF-8 SDDL string, the same value as sa-sync's `default-scope.json`). On that account the restore must succeed; on
any other account (CI runners included), the tests skip only the restore comparison and print `SKIPPED`.
